issue.summary: Same supplier on 2 different payment terms across ERPs

plan.diagnosis: Horizon United Metals AG operates across 3 ERP instances (SAP_A, NETSUITE, SAP_B) with inconsistent payment terms (NT60 and Net 30), creating a USD 8,607,604 spend exposure. The mismatch enables the supplier to exploit favorable terms selectively and introduces working capital inefficiency and compliance risk across the multi-ERP landscape.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct immediate three-way reconciliation of Horizon United Metals AG master data across SAP_A, NETSUITE, and SAP_B to document current payment term configurations (NT60 vs Net 30) and validate spend allocation by ERP instance
Negotiate unified payment terms with Horizon United Metals AG based on USD 8,607,604 annual spend leverage, targeting standardized Net 45 terms with 2% 10 early payment discount across all ERPs

Update supplier master records to harmonized terms: SAP_A and SAP_B via XK02 (vendor master change, LFB1 payment terms field ZTERM), NETSUITE via vendor record edit, document change rationale and effective date in all systems
Implement automated quarterly cross-ERP payment terms compliance audit using data extracts from SAP (LFB1-ZTERM), NETSUITE (Vendor.terms), and SAP_B with variance reporting to Procurement Operations
Establish global vendor governance policy requiring single payment term standard for all suppliers exceeding USD 5M annual spend, with MDM workflow approval for exceptions

plan.expected_impact: Standardizing payment terms across all ERPs will eliminate selective payment exploitation and improve Days Payable Outstanding (DPO) consistency, potentially capturing 1-2% early payment discount value on USD 8,607,604 spend (USD 86,076 to USD 172,152 annual benefit).
kpis: Payment term variance across ERPs for Horizon United Metals AG (target: 0 instances)
DPO consistency metric for supplier (target: <3 day variance across ERPs)
Early payment discount capture rate (target: 60% of invoices if 2% 10 implemented)
Master data governance compliance score (target: 100% for suppliers >USD 5M spend)
risks: Supplier resistance to less favorable unified terms may threaten USD 8,607,604 supply continuity for metals category
ERP system synchronization delays across SAP_A, NETSUITE, and SAP_B could create invoice processing disputes during transition
Incomplete master data remediation may leave payment term mismatches in subsidiary legal entities not covered in initial scope
Lack of ongoing governance may allow term drift to recur as new purchase orders are created across decentralized procurement teams

SAP_A and SAP_B: Create custom Z-report or BW query on LFB1-ZTERM joined to LFA1-LIFNR to monitor payment term consistency for suppliers >USD 5M spend monthly
